name: Color Contrast Checker
title: Color Contrast Checker: WCAG AA and AAA Ratio Test
description: Check the contrast ratio between text and background colors against WCAG 2 AA and AAA, preview the text, and get the nearest passing color. Runs in your browser.
card: Test text and background colors against WCAG AA and AAA.
lede: Pick a text and background color to get the WCAG contrast ratio, pass or fail for each level, and a suggested fix when it fails.
answer_q: What contrast ratio do I need for accessible text?
answer: WCAG 2 level AA needs at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (24 pixels, or about 18.66 pixels bold). Level AAA needs 7:1 and 4.5:1. Enter your colors to see your ratio.
steps: Enter or pick the text color.
Enter or pick the background color.
Read the ratio and the pass or fail table.
If normal text fails AA, try the suggested color.
Re-check hover, disabled and placeholder states too.

examples.title: Gray text on white
examples.output: 2.84:1. Fails AA for normal text. Suggested: a darker gray such as #767676 or darker.

faq.a: With the WCAG 2 formula: (lighter relative luminance + 0.05) divided by (darker + 0.05), using sRGB gamma-corrected luminance.

faq.q: Does placeholder text need to pass?
faq.a: WCAG applies contrast requirements to text that conveys information, which includes placeholder text people rely on to understand a field.
Check against the lightest and darkest parts of the image behind the text, or add a solid or semi-transparent overlay.

faq.q: Is this the same as WCAG 3 or APCA?
faq.a: No. This uses the WCAG 2 ratio, which is what current accessibility laws and audits reference.
